title: Mixtures and Solutions
seo_title: Grade 5 Mixtures and Solutions Worksheets: Separating Mixtures and Dissolving
standard_text: Make observations and measurements to identify materials based on their properties. Conduct an investigation to determine whether the mixing of two or more substances results in new substances.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on mixtures and solutions (NGSS 5-PS1-3, 5-PS1-4): solute and solvent, separating with a magnet, sieve, filter and evaporation, what makes things dissolve faster, and saturated solutions. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Separate a mixture by using the different properties of its parts.
key_sub: A solution is a mixture where one substance dissolves evenly in another. Filters cannot catch dissolved salt; evaporation can.
body_html:
How to think about it

A mixture is two or more substances put together. Each part keeps its own properties, so you can separate the parts by using those properties.

MixtureMethodProperty used
iron filings + sandmagnetattracted to a magnet
pebbles + sandsievesize
sand + waterfiltersize
salt dissolved in waterevaporate the watersolubility
wood chips + sandadd water, skimfloats or sinks

A solution is a mixture where one substance (the solute) dissolves evenly in another (the solvent), like sugar in water. Stirring, warmer water and smaller pieces make it dissolve faster. When no more can dissolve, the solution is saturated.

Example

How can you get salt back from salt water?

A filter will not work: the salt is dissolved.

Let the water evaporate.

Answer: Evaporate the water; the salt is left.

Example

30 g of sand is mixed with 200 g of water. What is the mass of the mixture?

Mixing does not add or remove matter.

30 + 200 = 230.

Answer: 230 g

Common mistakes

  • Trying to filter dissolved salt or sugar. Dissolved particles pass through a filter.
  • Thinking a dissolved solid is gone. It is still there, and so is its mass.
  • Thinking stirring lets any amount dissolve. Stirring only makes it faster.
  • Calling every mixture a solution. In a solution you cannot see the separate parts.

faq.q: What is the difference between a mixture and a solution?
faq.a: A mixture is two or more substances put together that keep their own properties. A solution is a kind of mixture where one substance dissolves evenly in another, like salt water.

faq.q: How do you separate salt from water?
faq.a: Let the water evaporate. A filter does not work because the salt is dissolved into particles small enough to pass through it.

faq.q: What makes a solid dissolve faster?
faq.a: Stirring, warmer water and smaller pieces. They do not change how much can dissolve, only how fast.
A solution that cannot dissolve any more solute. Extra solute stays at the bottom.

items.q: Which of these is a solution?
items.e: Vinegar has one substance dissolved evenly in water, so you cannot see the parts. The others are mixtures with parts you can see.

items.q: Which of these is a mixture but not a solution?
items.e: In trail mix you can still see the separate parts. Nothing is dissolved evenly.

items.q: Is every solution a mixture?
c: Yes. A solution is a special kind of mixture.

items.e: A solution is a mixture where one part is dissolved. The parts can still be separated, for example by evaporation.

items.e: In a solution the dissolved sugar spreads evenly through the tea.

items.e: Salt, sugar and many other substances dissolve in water.

items.q: What is a mixture?
c: only a liquid with something in it
two or more substances mixed together that keep their own properties
one new substance made from two
a substance that cannot be separated
items.e: In a mixture, each part keeps its own properties, so the parts can be separated again.

items.q: In salt water, the salt is the
c: solvent (the substance that does the dissolving)
items.e: The solute dissolves. The solvent, usually water, does the dissolving.

items.q: Why can the parts of a mixture be separated?
c: Each part keeps its own properties.
items.e: Different properties, like size, magnetism or solubility, let you pull the parts apart.

items.q: How can you separate a mixture of oil and water?
c: let it settle and pour off the top layer
items.e: Oil does not dissolve in water; it floats as a layer on top that can be poured or scooped off.

items.q: Why does a sieve separate pebbles from sand but not salt from water?
c: Salt in water is dissolved into particles far smaller than the holes.
items.e: A sieve only catches pieces bigger than its holes. Dissolved salt is far too small.

items.q: How can you separate a mixture of salt dissolved in water?
c: add water and skim off what floats
items.e: Salt is dissolved, so a filter cannot catch it. When the water evaporates, the salt is left.

items.q: Gold miners swirl sand and gold in a pan of water. The heavy gold stays at the bottom. Which property are they using?
c: Gold sinks faster and stays at the bottom.
items.e: Gold is much heavier for its size than sand, so it settles while water washes the sand away.

items.q: How can you separate a mixture of dried beans and flour?
c: add water and skim off what floats
let it settle and pour off the top layer
items.e: The flour falls through the sieve; the beans are too big.

items.q: How can you separate a mixture of mud and water?
c: let it settle and pour off the top layer
items.e: The filter catches the bits of soil and lets the water through.

items.q: To separate cork pieces and gravel, you add water and skim off what floats. Which property does this method use?
items.e: This method works because the parts differ in floating and sinking.

items.q: A mixture of sand, salt and iron filings needs three steps. What should you do first?
c: Pull out the iron filings with a magnet.
items.e: Magnet first (iron), then add water to dissolve the salt, filter out the sand, and evaporate the water to get the salt.

items.q: To separate dried beans and flour, you shake it through a sieve (screen). Which property does this method use?
items.e: This method works because the parts differ in particle size.

items.q: To separate sugar dissolved in water, you let the water evaporate. Which property does this method use?
items.e: This method works because the parts differ in solubility (it dissolves).

items.q: After you add water to sand and salt and filter it, what passes through the filter?
items.e: The salt dissolves, so it passes through with the water. The sand stays on the filter.

items.q: What is the best way to separate salt dissolved in water?
c: add water and skim off what floats
items.e: Salt is dissolved, so a filter cannot catch it. When the water evaporates, the salt is left.

items.q: Which method separates iron filings and sand?

c: Yes, if you use two filters.
Yes, the filter catches the salt.
No. The dissolved salt passes through the filter with the water.
Only if the water is cold.
items.e: Dissolved particles are too small to be caught. Evaporate the water to get the salt.

items.q: A coffee filter is used to make coffee. What does it separate?
c: the coffee grounds from the coffee drink
items.e: The grounds are too big to pass through. The water with dissolved coffee passes through.

items.q: How can you separate a mixture of cork pieces and gravel?
c: add water and skim off what floats
let it settle and pour off the top layer
items.e: Cork floats and gravel sinks.

Eli timed how long a sugar cube took to dissolve in water at different temperatures. What pattern does the data show?
c: Sugar does not dissolve in warm water.
The colder the water, the faster the sugar dissolves.
Temperature does not change the time.
The warmer the water, the faster the sugar dissolves.
items.e: As the temperature goes up from 10 °C to 40 °C, the time goes down from 183 s to 99 s.

items.q: Extra salt sits at the bottom of a saturated salt water solution. What could you do to dissolve more?
items.e: More water can hold more salt. Warming the water can also help some solids dissolve.

Why did Luis's granulated sugar dissolve faster than the cube?
c: Small pieces have more surface touching the water.
The cube is a different substance.

items.e: Breaking sugar into small grains lets more water touch it at once, so it dissolves faster (35 s instead of 187 s).

items.q: Does stirring change how much salt can dissolve in a cup of water?
c: Yes, stirring lets any amount dissolve.
Only if you stir for an hour.
No. It only makes it dissolve faster.
items.e: Stirring speeds things up, but the amount that can dissolve depends on the amount and temperature of the water.

items.q: Which three things make sugar dissolve faster in water?
c: cold water, big lumps and no stirring
stirring, warmer water and smaller pieces
items.e: All three help more water particles reach the sugar more often.

items.q: Why does a sugar cube dissolve faster in hot tea than in iced tea?
c: Hot tea has more sugar in it.
The water particles move faster and hit the sugar more often.
items.e: Faster-moving water particles pull the sugar particles away more quickly.

items.q: Sam adds 6-gram scoops of a powder to 200 mL of water and stirs after each one. The first 5 scoops dissolve. After scoop 6, powder stays at the bottom no matter how long he stirs. About how many grams dissolved?
items.e: 5 scoops × 6 g = 30 g. The solution is saturated: no more powder can dissolve in that much water.

items.q: Salt is dissolved in water and the salt seems to disappear. What happens to the total mass?
c: It goes down by the mass of the salt.

items.q: When the parts of a mixture are separated, how does their total mass compare with the mixture?
c: It is the same (if nothing is spilled or lost).
items.e: Separating does not create or destroy matter. Any difference comes from spills or water left on a filter.

items.q: Leo separates a salt and sand mixture. Which order of steps works?
c: add water, filter, evaporate the water
filter the dry mixture, then add water
items.e: Water dissolves the salt, the filter catches the sand, and evaporation leaves the salt.

items.q: Ava tests whether sugar dissolves faster in warm or cold water. What must stay the same?
c: only the color of the cups
the amount of sugar, the amount of water and the stirring
items.e: Only the temperature changes. Everything else stays the same so the test is fair.

items.q: Sea salt is made by letting seawater sit in shallow ponds in the sun. Which method is this?

items.q: A water treatment plant lets dirty water sit in a big tank so mud settles, then pours it through sand. Which separation methods are used?

items.q: Which result shows that mixing iron filings and sulfur powder did not make a new substance?
c: A magnet can still pull out the iron filings.
items.e: The iron kept its property of being attracted to a magnet, so it is still iron.

items.q: Omar stirs drink powder into water, and the water turns red. Is this a new substance?
c: Yes, because it cannot be separated.
No. It is a solution; the powder dissolved and spread its color.
items.e: Evaporating the water would leave the powder. Coloring water by dissolving is a physical change.

items.q: Noah wants to know which dissolves faster in water: salt or sugar. What should he change?

items.e: Testing one variable at a time shows which solid dissolves faster.
